newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm in late trade.

text.p: Singapore shares were firm in late trading on Tuesday hampered by a breakdown in the central computer of the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES), said dealers.
"The system broke down and we have not been able to key in any trades," said a dealer.
She said the system broke down about half an hour before the close at 0900 GMT. "We have wanted to see if they will extend trading but obviously they have not," said another trader.
A SES official said they were looking into the problem but could not give details. The Straits Times Industrial index was up 10.94 points to 2,128.17 in late trade.
Total volume was an active 100.7 million shares with 155 gainers against 138 losers.
An institutional dealer funds have not been able to complete their orders today and would probably have to continue tomorrow.
Japanese funds were seen picking up property and selective blue chip and bank stocks, dealers added.
Topping the actives was Kian Ann which was last traded at Singapore $0.945 (US$0.68) with 15.5 million shares traded.
DBS foreign, Rothmans and City Developments led the gainers, rising between S$0.50 and S$0.40 cents each while Creative and Total Access ended lower.
